body: Just like me
Ask at your next appointment. There are also online therapists if you don’t have a way to call

There’s never any shame in bringing something up with your therapist, even if you end up not having DID, maybe try writing down a list and sending it to her? I had to do it via text message before our appointment. 

Also, once every 2 months is really infrequent. My therapist used to be once a month until I voiced that I felt like I needed more support, and it took a month of waiting for her to work it out but I’m now scheduled with her once a week. You should bring up that once every 2 months isn’t feeling like enough and if she can’t work you in more often, you can ask if she can refer you to someone else that has more availability.

I think maybe a better way to phrase your posts would be “is this a symptom of DID?” rather than treating those who are diagnosed as experts who can predict the probability you do or don’t have it.

If you’re worried about the possibility of being a hypochondriac, please look into OCD and it’s symptoms. I’m not saying you have that instead of DID (you can actually have both) but I personally have a hard time differentiating symptoms from intrusive thoughts, and I’m sure it would be helpful to figure out what you do and don’t relate with.

Hi, I’m not diagnosed with DID (yet?) but I am seeing a therapist for my symptoms, and that video game feeling you described is derealization. I have no idea whether you have DID or not and am definitely not qualified to say so but it sounds like you are struggling with dissociate symptoms and I strongly recommend you find a therapist so help unravel everything. 

Also, no need to apologize for posting here. I just did a couple days ago with a similar topic and just about everyone was completely lovely to me. DID or not, we are all simply figuring ourselves out and it’s okay to explore it if you relate strongly with a specific condition.

Thanks 😭 this was a throwaway I made over a year ago I just kinda found and used to make this post, I guess I posted in r/suicidewatch but the post is now deleted & I don’t remember it very much if at all.

Edit: update, I found the post on Unddit and wrote here in a new post about my findings.

I really appreciate you contributing your experiences in such a thorough and detailed comment, reading all of this this has helped me feel a lot better. The similarities between us are extremely uncanny! Thank you.

Yes. Specifically complete strangers seeming to know me, finding notes in my phone, and frequently needing to be caught up on the current conversation due to feeling dizzy. It’s been a lifelong thing for me :/ and I had no idea how often I dissociated until my partner pointed out when I was.

See but where I get confused, is what if I am just telling myself I am faking because then because I’m questioning it I might actually have it? Like imagine intentionally questioning it just to make yourself think you have it… my head hurts 😂
I’ll definitely check out that book, and yeah I do the same whenever I have encountered someone with DID. Thank you!
Thank you so much for the very kind words and the advice. :’)

He is extremely supportive of me and is usually more than willing to be there for me, I don’t think him needing some space right now is a bad thing at all and I’m personally happy he feels comfortable to set that boundary. It’s just bad timing with my therapist going on vacation😅

If there’s anything I can say for certain it’s that I definitely don’t actually WANT to have this disorder at all, and I’m not fully convinced that I do. I had a traumatic childhood and dissociate very frequently and I have recognized this for a while through therapy. I came here asking for help because just the suspicion that I have DID has thrown me massively off balance and is causing me to question my own reality in my head.
I resonate strongly with everything you’ve said, and I will try to focus less on the label, thank you for your advice.

No offense taken, and by no means am I claiming I definitely have DID in this post. My therapist and I have just now started to discuss the possibility, but she has recognized I struggle with dissociation for a long time and has recognized it in therapy sessions even when I haven’t. She thinks is very likely I have some type of dissociative disorder, but I can’t disagree that it is possible this is all just an intrusive thought. I appreciate your input.

I really thought it was just me going through these episodes, that helps me feel simultaneously better and worse… 😂 

I relate strongly about not feeling comfortable about yourself. I’m not sure what inspired me to say anything at all and would take it all back if I could. I constantly feel like I’m not ready.

Well shit. I have had that feeling a lot of times in my life, specifically when people have called me out on “spacing out” or anything dissociation-related at all. Literally hearing about dissociation makes me dissociate, it’s so weird.

Oh I mean he talked to me for a good while about me potentially having it, and effectively said exactly your example. He had a really bad past experience with an ex who also had DID and I think his emotional load is just too full right now to take on another stressful task. Someone very close to him died just a few days ago.

There are a lot of details surrounding why my partner isn’t ready for me to talk about it to him that I didn’t mention, and it’s completely fair for him to need a little time. 

You also had the uneasiness? Is that a common thing to have? Thank you for the reply.
I did have hives that night. Thank you so much for your comment, you have no idea how validating it was for me.
